title.zh: 卷一百十五 列傳第四十五: 二國外記
title.en: Volume 115 Biographies 45: Two Records of Foreign Countries
title.raw: 卷一百十五 列傳第四十五: 二國外記 Volume 115 Biographies 45: Two Records of Foreign Countries

sentences.zh: 高麗自有國以來，傳次久近，人民土田，歷代各有其志，然高麗與遼，相為終始二百餘年。

translations.literal: Since Goryeo had its own state, the order of succession had been long or short, and its people, land, and fields each generation had their own ambitions; yet Goryeo and Liao were bound to each other from beginning to end for more than two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Goryeo became a kingdom, its dynastic lines rose and fell at different intervals, and generation after generation its people and territory pursued their own aims; yet Goryeo and Liao remained entwined with one another for more than two hundred years, from first to last.

sentences.zh: 自太祖皇帝神冊間，高麗遣使進寶劍。

translations.literal: From the Shence era of Emperor Taizu, Goryeo sent envoys presenting a treasured sword.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shence reign of Emperor Taizu, Goryeo dispatched envoys bearing a treasured sword as tribute.

sentences.zh: 天贊三年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianzan, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianzan, they sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 太宗天顯二年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxian of Emperor Taizong, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianxian under Emperor Taizong, they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 會同二年，受晉上尊號冊，遣使往報。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huitong, having received the honorific title register from Jin, he sent envoys to report it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huitong, after receiving the honorific title register from Jin, the court sent envoys to inform Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 聖宗統和三年秋七月，詔諸道各完戎器，以備東征高麗。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn of the third year of Tonghe of Emperor Shengzong, an edict ordered each circuit to complete weapons in preparation for an eastern expedition against Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn in the third year of Tonghe, Emperor Shengzong ordered every circuit to ready its arms in preparation for a campaign east against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 八月，以遼澤沮洳，罷師。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, because the Liao marshes were waterlogged, the army was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the expedition was called off, the Liao marshes being too boggy to advance.

sentences.zh: 十年，以東京留守蕭恒德伐高麗。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Xiao Hengde, Eastern Capital garrison commander, attacked Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Xiao Hengde, regent of the Eastern Capital, led a campaign against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 十一年，王治遣樸良柔奉表請罪，詔取女直國鴨淥江東數百里地賜之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Wang Che sent Park Yang-yu with a memorial pleading guilt; an edict took several hundred li of land east of the Yalu River in the Jurchen state and granted it to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, King Wang Che sent Park Yang-yu with a memorial submitting to judgment; the court decreed that several hundred li of territory east of the Yalu River in Jurchen lands be granted to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 十二年，入貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, Goryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 三月，王治遣使請所俘生口，詔贖還之，仍遣使撫諭。

translations.literal: In the third month, Wang Che sent envoys requesting the captives taken alive; an edict ordered them ransomed and returned, and envoys were still sent to comfort and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Wang Che asked for the return of captives taken alive; the court ordered them ransomed and sent back, and dispatched envoys to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，王治進妓樂，詔卻之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Wang Che presented singing girls and musicians; an edict refused them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Wang Che offered female entertainers and musicians; the court declined the gift.

sentences.zh: 十三年，治遣李周楨來貢，又進鷹。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Che sent Li Zhouzhen to offer tribute, and also presented hawks.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Wang Che sent Li Zhouzhen with tribute and also presented hunting hawks.

sentences.zh: 十月，遣李知白奉貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he sent Li Zhibai to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, he sent Li Zhibai bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣使冊治為王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, envoys were sent to invest Che as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, the court dispatched envoys to invest Wang Che as king of Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 遣童子十人來學本國語。

translations.literal: Ten youths were sent to study the language of our state.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo sent ten youths to study the Khitan language.

sentences.zh: 十四年，王治表乞為婚姻，以東京留守駙馬蕭恒德女下嫁之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Wang Che memorialized requesting a marriage alliance; the daughter of Xiao Hengde, Eastern Capital garrison commander and imperial son-in-law, was given in marriage to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Wang Che petitioned for a marriage alliance, and the daughter of Xiao Hengde, garrison commander of the Eastern Capital and an imperial son-in-law, was given to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣使來問起居。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, envoys were sent to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Goryeo sent envoys to inquire after the emperor's well-being.

sentences.zh: 自是至者無時。

translations.literal: From this time onward, arrivals were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, envoys arrived without pause.

sentences.zh: 十五年，韓彥敬來納聘幣，弔駙馬蕭恒德妻越國公主薨。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Han Yanjing came to present betrothal gifts and mourn the death of the Yue State Princess, wife of Imperial Son-in-law Xiao Hengde.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Han Yanjing came with betrothal gifts to mourn the Yue State Princess, wife of Imperial Son-in-law Xiao Hengde.

sentences.zh: 十一月，治薨，其姪誦遣王同穎來告。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Che died; his nephew Song sent Wang Tongying to announce it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Wang Che died; his nephew Wang Song sent Wang Tongying to report the death.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遣使致祭，詔其姪誦權知國事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, envoys were sent to offer sacrifices, and an edict ordered his nephew Song to provisionally administer state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Liao sent envoys to offer sacrifices and decreed that his nephew Wang Song should provisionally govern the state.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遣使冊誦為王。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, envoys were sent to invest Song as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, Liao sent envoys to invest Wang Song as king.

sentences.zh: 二十年，誦遣使賀伐宋之捷。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Song sent envoys to congratulate the victory over Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, Wang Song sent envoys to congratulate Liao on its victory over Song.

sentences.zh: 七月，來貢本國地里圖。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, they came to present a territorial map of their state.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Goryeo presented a map of its territory as tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，以南伐事詔諭之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, an edict was sent to instruct them concerning the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, Liao issued an edict instructing Goryeo concerning the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，高麗聞與宋和，遣使來賀。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Goryeo heard of peace with Song and sent envoys to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, hearing that Liao had made peace with Song, Goryeo sent envoys to congratulate.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，進龍鬚草席，及賀中京城。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, they presented dragon-whisker grass mats and congratulated on the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, they presented dragon-whisker grass mats and sent congratulations on the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，承天皇太后崩，遣使報以國哀。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Empress Dowager Chengtian died; envoys were sent to announce the state mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, after Empress Dowager Chengtian died, Goryeo sent envoys to announce its mourning.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，誦遣魏守愚等來祭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, Song sent Wei Shouyu and others to offer sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, Wang Song sent Wei Shouyu and others to offer sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 三月，使來會葬。

translations.literal: In the third month, envoys came to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Goryeo sent envoys to attend the funeral.

sentences.zh: 五月，高麗西京留守康肇弒其主誦，擅立誦從兄詢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Kang Cho, Western Capital garrison commander of Goryeo, murdered his lord Song and on his own authority established Song's cousin Seon as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Kang Cho, garrison commander of Goryeo's Western Capital, assassinated King Wang Song and installed Song's cousin Wang Seon as king without authorization.

sentences.zh: 八月，聖宗自將伐高麗，報宋，遣引進使韓杞宣問詢。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Emperor Shengzong personally led a campaign against Goryeo, informed Song, and sent Introducing Commissioner Han Qi to announce and question Seon.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Emperor Shengzong led the campaign against Goryeo in person, notified the Song court, and sent Introducing Commissioner Han Qi to confront Wang Seon.

sentences.zh: 詢奉表乞罷師，不許。

translations.literal: Seon submitted a memorial begging that the army be withdrawn; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Seon submitted a memorial pleading for withdrawal of the army; the request was refused.

sentences.zh: 十一月，大軍渡鴨淥江，康肇拒戰於銅州，敗之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the great army crossed the Yalu River; Kang Cho resisted at Tong Prefecture and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the main force crossed the Yalu River; Kang Cho made a stand at Tong Prefecture and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 肇復出，右皮室詳穩耶律敵魯擒肇等，追奔數十里，獲所棄糧餉、鎧仗，銅、霍、貴、寧等州皆降。

translations.literal: Cho came out again; Yelu Dilu, detailed commander of the Right Pishi Army, captured Cho and others, pursued the flight for several tens of li, seized abandoned provisions and armor, and Tong, Huo, Gui, Ning, and other prefectures all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Kang Cho sallied forth again, Yelu Dilu, detailed commander of the Right Pishi Army, captured him and his followers, pursued the fleeing enemy for dozens of li, and seized abandoned supplies and arms; Tong, Huo, Gui, Ning, and other prefectures all submitted.

sentences.zh: 詢上表請朝，許之，禁軍士俘掠。

translations.literal: Seon submitted a memorial requesting an audience; it was granted, and the troops were forbidden to seize captives or plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Seon petitioned for permission to come to court; the request was granted, and the troops were forbidden to take captives or loot.

sentences.zh: 以政事舍人馬保祐為開京留守，安州團練使王八為副留守。

translations.literal: Ma Baoyou, Administrative Affairs Attendant, was made Kaesong garrison commander, and Wang Ba, militia commissioner of An Prefecture, was made deputy garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Baoyou, an Administrative Affairs Attendant, was appointed garrison commander of Kaesong, with Wang Ba, militia commissioner of An Prefecture, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 太子太師乙凜將騎兵一千，送保祐等赴京。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Yi Lin led one thousand cavalry to escort Baoyou and the others to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Yi Lin led a thousand horsemen to escort Ma Baoyou and his party to Kaesong.

sentences.zh: 守將卓思正殺我使者韓喜孫等十人，領兵出拒，保祐等復還。

translations.literal: The defending general Zhuo Sizheng killed our envoys Han Xisun and nine others, led troops out to resist, and Baoyou and the others returned.
translations.idiomatic: The defending general Zhuo Sizheng killed ten of our envoys, including Han Xisun, marched out to resist, and Ma Baoyou's party was forced to turn back.

sentences.zh: 乙凜領兵擊之，思正遂奔西京。

translations.literal: Yi Lin led troops to attack him, and Sizheng then fled to the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Lin attacked him, and Zhuo Sizheng fled to the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 圍之五日，不克，駐蹕於城西佛寺。

translations.literal: They besieged it for five days without taking it, and the imperial presence halted at a Buddhist temple west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: After a five-day siege that failed to capture the city, the emperor encamped at a Buddhist temple west of the walls.

sentences.zh: 高麗禮部郎中渤海陀失來降。

translations.literal: Bohai Tuoshi, Director in the Ministry of Rites of Goryeo, came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Bohai Tuoshi, a director in Goryeo's Ministry of Rites, came over to the Liao side.

sentences.zh: 遣排押、盆奴攻開京，遇敵於京西，敗之。

translations.literal: Paiya and Pennu were sent to attack Kaesong; they met the enemy west of the capital and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Paiya and Pennu were dispatched to attack Kaesong; west of the capital they met the enemy and routed them.

sentences.zh: 詢棄城遁走，遂焚開京，至清江而還。

translations.literal: Seon abandoned the city and fled; they then burned Kaesong and returned as far as the Qing River.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Seon abandoned the city and fled; the Liao forces burned Kaesong and withdrew as far as the Qing River.

sentences.zh: 二十九年正月，班師，所降諸城復叛。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-ninth year, the army withdrew; the cities that had surrendered rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-ninth year the army withdrew, and the cities that had submitted rose in revolt again.

sentences.zh: 至貴州南嶺谷，大雨連日，霽乃得渡，馬駝皆疲乏，甲仗多遺棄。

translations.literal: When they reached Southern Ridge Valley in Gui Prefecture, heavy rain fell for days on end; only when it cleared could they cross; horses and camels were all exhausted, and much armor and weapons were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: At Southern Ridge Valley in Gui Prefecture, days of torrential rain held them up; only when the skies cleared could they cross. Horses and camels were spent, and much armor and weaponry had to be left behind.

sentences.zh: 次鴨淥江，以所俘人分置諸陵廟，余賜內戚、大臣。

translations.literal: They halted at the Yalu River; the captives were distributed among the imperial tombs and temples, and the remainder were given to inner kin and great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at the Yalu River; captives were apportioned among the imperial mausoleums and temples, and the rest were bestowed on imperial relatives and high officials.

sentences.zh: 開泰元年，詢遣蔡忠順來乞稱臣如舊，詔詢親朝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaitai, Seon sent Cai Zhongshun to beg to submit as a subject as before; an edict ordered Seon to come to court in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaitai, Wang Seon sent Cai Zhongshun to plead for restoration of his former subject status; the court ordered him to appear in person.

sentences.zh: 八月，遣田拱之奉表，稱病不能朝。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Tian Gongzhi was sent with a memorial, claiming illness and inability to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Tian Gongzhi was sent with a memorial claiming illness and inability to come to court.

sentences.zh: 詔復取六州之地。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the six prefectures' territory to be taken back again.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the recovery of the six prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二年，耶律資忠使高麗取地，未幾還。

translations.literal: In the second year, Yelu Zizhong was sent to Goryeo to take the territory; before long he returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Yelu Zizhong was sent to Goryeo to reclaim the territory; he returned before long.

sentences.zh: 三年，資忠復使，如前索地。

translations.literal: In the third year, Zizhong was sent again, demanding the territory as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Zizhong was sent again to demand the territory on the same terms.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔國舅詳穩蕭敵烈、東京留守耶律團石等造浮梁於鴨淥江，城保、宣義、定遠等州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, an edict ordered the imperial maternal uncle's detailed commander Xiao Dilie, Eastern Capital garrison commander Yelu Tuanshi, and others to build a pontoon bridge on the Yalu River and fortify Bao, Xuanyi, Dingyuan, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the court ordered Xiao Dilie, detailed commander of the imperial maternal uncle's command, Yelu Tuanshi, garrison commander of the Eastern Capital, and others to build a pontoon bridge across the Yalu and to wall the prefectures of Bao, Xuanyi, Dingyuan, and the like.

sentences.zh: 四年，命北府宰相劉慎行為都統，樞密使耶律世良為副，殿前都點檢蕭虛烈為都監。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Northern Chancellery Chancellor Liu Shenxing was appointed commander-in-chief, Privy Commissioner Yelu Shiliang was made deputy, and Palace Front Commander Xiao Xulie was made chief overseer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Liu Shenxing, chancellor of the Northern Chancellery, was appointed commander-in-chief; Privy Commissioner Yelu Shiliang was made his deputy; and Palace Front Commander Xiao Xulie was made chief overseer.

sentences.zh: 慎行挈家邊上，致緩師期，追還之，以世良、虛烈總兵伐高麗。

translations.literal: Shenxing brought his family to the frontier, causing delay in the campaign schedule; he was recalled, and Shiliang and Xulie took overall command to attack Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing brought his household to the frontier and thereby delayed the campaign; he was recalled, and Shiliang and Xulie were placed in overall command of the attack on Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 五年，世良等與高麗戰於郭州西，破之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Shiliang and the others fought Goryeo west of Guo Prefecture and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Shiliang and his forces defeated the Goryeo army west of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年，樞密使蕭合卓為都統，漢人行宮都部署王繼忠為副，殿前都點檢蕭虛烈為都監進討。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Privy Commissioner Xiao Hezhuo was made commander-in-chief, Han Palace Mobile Command Director Wang Jizhong was made deputy, and Palace Front Commander Xiao Xulie was made chief overseer to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Privy Commissioner Xiao Hezhuo was appointed commander-in-chief, Wang Jizhong, director of the Han mobile palace command, was made deputy, and Palace Front Commander Xiao Xulie was made chief overseer for the advance.

sentences.zh: 蕭合卓攻興化軍不克，師還。

translations.literal: Xiao Hezhuo attacked Xinghua Army but could not take it, and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hezhuo besieged Xinghua Army without success, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔東平郡王蕭排押為都統，蕭虛烈為副統，東京留守耶律八哥為都監，復伐高麗。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict appointed Eastern Peace Prince Xiao Paiya commander-in-chief, Xiao Xulie deputy commander, and Eastern Capital garrison commander Yelu Bage chief overseer to attack Goryeo again.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Eastern Peace Prince Xiao Paiya was appointed commander-in-chief, Xiao Xulie deputy commander, and Yelu Bage, garrison commander of the Eastern Capital, chief overseer for another campaign against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 十二月，蕭排押與戰於茶、陀二河之間，我軍不利，天雲、右皮室二軍沒溺者眾，天雲軍詳穩海裏、遙輦帳詳穩阿果達、客省使酌古、渤海詳穩高清明等皆沒於陣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xiao Paiya fought between the Cha and Tuo rivers; our army was unfavorable; many of the Tianyun and Right Pishi armies were drowned; Tianyun Army detailed commander Haili, Yaolian Account detailed commander Aguoda, Reception Commissioner Zhuogu, Bohai detailed commander Gao Qingming, and others all perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Xiao Paiya engaged the enemy between the Cha and Tuo rivers. Our forces fared badly: many men of the Tianyun and Right Pishi armies were drowned. Detailed commanders Haili of the Tianyun Army, Aguoda of the Yaolian Account, Reception Commissioner Zhuogu, Bohai detailed commander Gao Qingming, and others all fell in the field.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔數排押討高麗罪，釋之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict several times recounted Paiya's offenses in the Goryeo campaign and then pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the court listed Xiao Paiya's offenses in the Goryeo campaign and then pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 加有功將校，益封戰沒將校之妻，錄其子弟。

translations.literal: Meritorious officers were promoted in rank; the wives of officers who died in battle received additional enfeoffment, and their sons and younger brothers were entered on the register.
translations.idiomatic: Officers who had distinguished themselves were promoted; the wives of officers killed in battle received additional grants of rank, and their sons and younger brothers were enrolled for office.

sentences.zh: 以南皮室軍校有功，賜衣物銀絹有差，出金帛賜肴裏、涅哥二奚軍。

translations.literal: Because officers of the Southern Pishi Army had merit, clothing, silver, and silk were bestowed in graded amounts; gold and silks were issued to reward the Yaoli and Niege Xi armies.
translations.idiomatic: Officers of the Southern Pishi Army who had performed well were rewarded with graded gifts of clothing, silver, and silk; gold and silk were also distributed to the Yaoli and Niege Xi armies.

sentences.zh: 八月，遣郎君曷不呂等率諸部兵，會大軍同討高麗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Gentleman Habuli and others were sent to lead the troops of the various commands to join the great army in a joint campaign against Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Habuli and other commanders were sent to lead the forces of the various commands in joining the main army for a joint campaign against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 詢遣使來乞貢方物。

translations.literal: Seon sent envoys to beg to offer local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Seon sent envoys asking permission to resume tribute of local products.

sentences.zh: 九年，資忠還，以詢降表進，釋詢罪。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Zizhong returned and presented Seon's surrender memorial; Seon's offenses were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Zizhong returned with Wang Seon's submission; the court accepted his surrender and pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 太平元年，詢薨，遣使來報嗣位，即遣使冊王欽為王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiping, Seon died; envoys were sent to report the succession, and envoys were immediately sent to invest Wang Qin as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiping, Wang Seon died; Goryeo sent envoys to announce the succession, and the court at once dispatched envoys to invest Wang Qin as king.

sentences.zh: 九年，賜欽物。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, gifts were bestowed on Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, the court bestowed gifts on Wang Qin.

sentences.zh: 十一年，聖宗崩，遣使告哀。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Emperor Shengzong died; envoys were sent to announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Emperor Shengzong died, and Goryeo sent envoys to announce the mourning.

sentences.zh: 七月，使來慰奠。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, envoys came to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Goryeo sent envoys to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 興宗重熙七年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongxi of Emperor Xingzong, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Chongxi under Emperor Xingzong, Goryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，以加上尊號，來賀。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twelfth year, because of the bestowal of an honorific title, they came to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twelfth year, Goryeo sent envoys to congratulate the court on the bestowal of an honorific title.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, envoys were sent to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Goryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十四年三月，又來貢。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourteenth year, they came to offer tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourteenth year, tribute came again.

sentences.zh: 十五年，入貢。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Goryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 八月，王欽薨，遣使來告。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Wang Qin died; envoys were sent to report it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Wang Qin died, and Goryeo sent envoys to announce his death.

sentences.zh: 十六年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, Goryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 明年，又來貢。

translations.literal: The next year, they came to offer tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, tribute came again.

sentences.zh: 十九年，復貢。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, tribute was offered again.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, tribute was sent once more.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣使來賀伐夏之捷。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, envoys were sent to congratulate the victory over Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Goryeo sent envoys to congratulate the victory over Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，入貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, Goryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十三年四月，王徽請官其子，詔加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-third year, Wang Hui requested an office for his son; an edict added Honorary Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-third year, Wang Hui asked that his son be given an office; the court granted him the honorary title of Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 興宗崩，道宗即位，清寧元年八月，遣使報國哀，以先帝遺留物賜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xingzong died and Emperor Daozong succeeded; in the eighth month of the first year of Qingning, envoys were sent to announce the national mourning, and objects left by the late emperor were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xingzong died and Emperor Daozong succeeded, Goryeo sent envoys in the eighth month of the first year of Qingning to announce the mourning; the court bestowed goods left by the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 十一月，使來會葬。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, envoys came to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Goryeo sent envoys to attend the funeral.

sentences.zh: 二年、三年，皆來貢。

translations.literal: In the second and third years, they all came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second and third years, Goryeo sent tribute both years.

sentences.zh: 四年春，遣使報太皇太后哀。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, envoys were sent to announce the Grand Empress Dowager's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year, Goryeo sent envoys to announce the death of the Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 五月，使來會葬。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, envoys came to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, envoys came to attend her funeral.

sentences.zh: 咸雍七年、八年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh and eighth years of Xianyong, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh and eighth years of Xianyong, Goryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以佛經一藏賜徽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, one complete canon of Buddhist scriptures was bestowed on Hui.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, the court presented Wang Hui with a complete set of Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 九年、十年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth and tenth years, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth and tenth years, Goryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 大康二年三月，皇太后崩，遣使報哀。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Dakang, the Empress Dowager died; envoys were sent to announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Dakang, the Empress Dowager died, and Goryeo sent envoys to announce the mourning.

sentences.zh: 六月，使來弔祭。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, envoys came to offer mourning sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, envoys came to perform mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 四年，王徽乞賜鴨淥江以東地，不許。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Wang Hui begged that land east of the Yalu River be granted; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Wang Hui asked for territory east of the Yalu River; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 九年八月，王徽薨，以徽子三韓國公勛權知國事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the ninth year, Wang Hui died; Hui's son, Three Han State Duke Xun, was made to administer state affairs provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the ninth year, Wang Hui died; his son Xun, Duke of the Three Han State, was appointed provisional regent.

sentences.zh: 十二月，勛薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xun died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Xun died as well.

sentences.zh: 大安元年，冊勛子運為國王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Da'an, Xun's son Yun was invested as king of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Da'an, Xun's son Yun was invested as king of Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣使來謝封冊。

translations.literal: In the second year, envoys were sent to thank for the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Goryeo sent envoys to thank the court for the investiture.

sentences.zh: 三年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Goryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，免歲貢。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year, the annual tribute was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year, the court exempted Goryeo from its annual tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年、六年，連貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth and sixth years, tribute was offered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth and sixth years, Goryeo sent tribute two years running.

sentences.zh: 九年，賜王運羊。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, sheep were bestowed on King Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, the court presented King Yun with sheep.

sentences.zh: 十年，運薨，子昱遣使來告，即賻贈。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Yun died; his son Yu sent envoys to report it, and funeral gifts were immediately bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Yun died; his son Yu sent envoys to announce the death, and the court at once sent funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 壽隆元年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shoulong, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shoulong, Goryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十一月，王昱病，命其子颙權知國事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Wang Yu fell ill and ordered his son Yong to administer state affairs provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Wang Yu fell ill and appointed his son Yong provisional regent.

sentences.zh: 二年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Goryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，王昱薨。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year, Wang Yu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year, Wang Yu died.

sentences.zh: 五年，王顒乞封冊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Wang Yong begged for investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Wang Yong petitioned for formal investiture.

sentences.zh: 六年，封顒為三韓國公。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Yong was enfeoffed as Duke of the Three Han State.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Yong was enfeoffed as Duke of the Three Han State.

sentences.zh: 七年，道宗崩，天祚即位，改為乾統元年，報道宗哀，使來慰奠。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Emperor Daozong died and Tianzuo succeeded; the era was changed to the first year of Qiantong; Daozong's mourning was announced, and envoys came to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Emperor Daozong died and Tianzuo succeeded, changing the era to Qiantong 1; Goryeo announced the mourning, and Liao envoys came to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遣使來賀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, envoys were sent to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Goryeo sent envoys to congratulate the new reign.

sentences.zh: 五年，三韓國公颙薨，子俁遣使來告。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Three Han State Duke Yong died; his son Hou sent envoys to report it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Duke Yong of the Three Han State died; his son Hou sent envoys to announce the death.

sentences.zh: 八年，封俁為三韓國公，贈其父颙為國王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Hou was enfeoffed as Duke of the Three Han State, and his father Yong was posthumously granted the title of king of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Hou was enfeoffed as Duke of the Three Han State, and his father Yong was posthumously honored as king.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遣使來謝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, envoys were sent to offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Goryeo sent envoys to express thanks.

sentences.zh: 九年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Goryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 天慶二年，王俁母薨，來告，遣使致祭，起復。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqing, Wang Hou's mother died; they came to report it; envoys were sent to offer sacrifices, and mourning leave was ended.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqing, the mother of Wang Hou died; Goryeo sent word, and the court dispatched envoys to perform sacrifices and ordered Hou to leave mourning.

sentences.zh: 三年，遣使來謝致祭，又來謝起復。

translations.literal: In the third year, envoys were sent to thank for the sacrifices, and again to thank for ending mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Goryeo sent envoys to thank the court for performing the sacrifices and again to thank for the order to leave mourning.

sentences.zh: 十年，乞兵於高麗以禦金，而金人責之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, troops were requested from Goryeo to resist Jin, and the Jin people held them accountable.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Liao asked Goryeo for troops to resist the Jin, and the Jin held Goryeo responsible.

sentences.zh: 至是遼國亡矣。

translations.literal: At this point the Liao state perished.
translations.idiomatic: With that, the Liao state came to an end.

sentences.zh: ○西夏

translations.literal: ○ Western Xia
translations.idiomatic: ○ Western Xia

sentences.zh: 西夏，本魏拓跋氏後，其地則赫連國也。

translations.literal: Western Xia were originally descendants of the Tuoba clan of Wei; their territory was the state of Helian.
translations.idiomatic: Western Xia descended from the Tuoba clan of Northern Wei; their lands had once been the realm of Helian Bobo.

sentences.zh: 遠祖思恭，唐季受賜姓曰李，涉五代至宋，世有其地。

translations.literal: Their remote ancestor Sigong, in the late Tang received the granted surname Li; passing through the Five Dynasties to Song, they held their territory for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Their remote ancestor Sigong received the surname Li from the Tang court in its final years; through the Five Dynasties and into Song, his line held the same territory generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 至李繼遷始大，據夏、銀、綏、宥、靜五州，緣境七鎮，其東西二十五驛，南北十餘驛。

translations.literal: When Li Jiqian first grew great, he held the five prefectures of Xia, Yin, Sui, You, and Jing, seven border garrisons along the frontier, twenty-five courier stations east and west, and more than ten stations north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Under Li Jiqian the state first rose to power, holding the five prefectures of Xia, Yin, Sui, You, and Jing, seven border garrisons, twenty-five courier stations east to west, and more than ten north to south.

sentences.zh: 子德明，曉佛書，通法律，嘗觀《太一金鑒訣》、《野戰歌》，制番書十二卷，又制字若符篆。

translations.literal: His son Deming understood Buddhist texts and was versed in law; he once studied the Taiyi Golden Mirror Formula and the Field Battle Songs, compiled twelve fascicles of Tangut script, and also devised characters like seal script.
translations.idiomatic: His son Deming was learned in Buddhist texts and versed in law; he studied works such as the Taiyi Golden Mirror Formula and the Field Battle Songs, compiled twelve fascicles in the Tangut script, and devised a writing system resembling seal characters.

sentences.zh: 其俗，衣白窄衫，氈冠，冠後垂紅結綬。

translations.literal: Their custom was to wear white narrow shirts and felt caps, with red knotted cords hanging down behind the cap.
translations.idiomatic: In dress they wore white narrow shirts and felt caps with red knotted cords hanging down behind.

sentences.zh: 自號嵬名，設官分文武。

translations.literal: They styled themselves Weiming and established offices dividing civil and military.
translations.idiomatic: They took the title Weiming and organized government into civil and military offices.

sentences.zh: 其冠用金縷貼，間起雲，銀紙帖，緋衣，金塗銀帶，佩蹀躞、解錐、短刀、弓矢，穿靴，禿發，耳重環，紫旋襕六襲。

translations.literal: Their caps used gold thread appliqué with cloud motifs between, silver paper appliqué, scarlet robes, gold-plated silver belts; they wore gaiters, awl-pouches, short knives, bow and arrows, boots, shaved their heads, heavy ear-rings, and six layers of purple spiral-lapel robes.
translations.idiomatic: Official caps were adorned with gold-thread cloud motifs and silver appliqué; they wore scarlet robes, gold-plated silver belts, gaiters, awl-pouches, short knives, bows and arrows, and boots; they shaved the head, wore heavy ear-rings, and donned six layers of purple spiral-lapel robes.

sentences.zh: 出入乘馬，張青蓋，以二旗前引，從者百餘騎。

translations.literal: Going out and coming in they rode horses, spread blue canopies, had two banners lead the way in front, and more than a hundred horsemen followed.
translations.idiomatic: They traveled on horseback beneath blue canopies, preceded by two banners, with more than a hundred mounted attendants.

sentences.zh: 民庶衣青綠。

translations.literal: The common people wore blue-green.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners dressed in blue-green.

sentences.zh: 革樂之五音為一音，裁禮之九拜為三拜。

translations.literal: They reduced the five tones of leather music to one tone, and trimmed the nine bows of ritual to three bows.
translations.idiomatic: They compressed the five tones of their leather music into one, and reduced the nine ritual prostrations to three.

sentences.zh: 凡出兵先卜，有四：一炙勃焦，以艾灼羊胛骨；

translations.literal: Whenever they took the field they divined first; there were four methods: first, scorching the shoulder blade, burning a sheep's shoulder blade with moxa;
translations.idiomatic: Before any campaign they divined by four methods: first, scorching the shoulder blade—burning a sheep's shoulder blade with moxa;

sentences.zh: 二擗算，擗竹於地以求數，若揲蓍然；

translations.literal: second, splitting counting rods, splitting bamboo on the ground to obtain numbers, like casting yarrow stalks;
translations.idiomatic: second, splitting counting rods—breaking bamboo on the ground to obtain numbers, as with yarrow stalks;

sentences.zh: 三咒羊，其夜牽羊，焚香禱之，又焚谷火於野，次晨屠羊，腸胃通則吉，羊心有血則敗；

translations.literal: third, cursing the sheep: that night they led out a sheep, burned incense and prayed to it, also burned grain fires in the wild; the next morning they slaughtered the sheep—if the entrails were clear it was auspicious, if there was blood in the sheep's heart it was defeat;
translations.idiomatic: third, the sheep curse—at night they led out a sheep, burned incense and prayed, and kindled grain fires in the open; at dawn they slaughtered it: clear entrails meant good fortune, blood in the heart meant defeat;

sentences.zh: 四矢擊弦，聽其聲，知勝負及敵至之期。

translations.literal: fourth, striking the bowstring with an arrow and listening to the sound to know victory or defeat and the time the enemy would arrive.
translations.idiomatic: fourth, striking the bowstring with an arrow and listening to the sound to learn victory or defeat and when the enemy would come.

sentences.zh: 病者不用醫藥，召巫者送鬼，西夏語以巫為「廝」也；

translations.literal: The sick did not use medicine but summoned shamans to send off ghosts; in the Tangut language shamans were called "si";
translations.idiomatic: The sick did not use medicine but called shamans to drive off spirits—the Tangut word for shaman was "si";

sentences.zh: 或遷他室，謂之「閃病」。

translations.literal: or they moved to another room, which was called "flashing illness."
translations.idiomatic: or they moved to another dwelling, which they called "flashing illness."

sentences.zh: 喜報仇，有喪則不伐人，負甲葉於背識之。

translations.literal: They delighted in revenge; when in mourning they did not attack others, and they bore leaves of armor on the back as a mark.
translations.idiomatic: They were eager for vengeance; while in mourning they refrained from raiding, marking themselves by wearing armor leaves on the back.

sentences.zh: 仇解，用雞豬犬血和酒，貯於髑髏中飲之，乃誓曰：「若復報仇，穀麥不收，男女禿癩，六畜死，蛇入帳。」

translations.literal: When enmity was resolved, they mixed chicken, pig, and dog blood with wine, stored it in a skull and drank it, then swore: "If we take revenge again, grain and wheat will not be harvested, men and women will go bald and leprous, the six livestock will die, and snakes will enter the tent."
translations.idiomatic: To end a feud they mixed the blood of chicken, pig, and dog with wine, drank it from a skull, and swore: "If we take revenge again, grain will fail, men and women will go bald and leprous, livestock will die, and snakes will enter our tents."

sentences.zh: 有力小不能復仇者，集壯婦，享以牛羊酒食，趨讎家縱火，焚其廬舍。

translations.literal: Those with little strength who could not take revenge gathered strong women, feasted them with cattle, sheep, food, and wine, and rushed to the enemy's house to set fire and burn their dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Those too weak to exact revenge themselves gathered strong women, feasted them with cattle, sheep, food, and wine, and sent them to the enemy's home to set fire and burn the dwellings.

sentences.zh: 俗曰敵女兵不祥，輒避去。

translations.literal: Custom said enemy women's troops were inauspicious, and they always avoided them.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, enemy women warriors were considered ill-omened, and troops always gave way before them.

sentences.zh: 訴於官，官擇舌辯氣直之人為和斷，官聽其屈直。

translations.literal: When they appealed to officials, officials chose men eloquent and upright in spirit to mediate and decide; officials listened to right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: When parties brought suits to officials, the court chose eloquent and upright men to mediate, judging the merits of each side.

sentences.zh: 殺人者，納命價錢百二十千。

translations.literal: For killing a person, one paid a life-price of one hundred twenty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: A killer paid a life-price of one hundred twenty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 土產大麥、蓽豆、青稞、𢇲子、古子蔓、鹹地蓬實、蓯蓉苗、小蕪荑、席雞草子、地黃葉、登廂草、沙葱、野韭、拒灰蓧、白蒿、鹹地松實。

translations.literal: Local products included barley, lablab beans, highland barley, haozi, guziman, salt-land purslane seeds, cistanche shoots, small elm fruits, mat-chicken grass seeds, rehmannia leaves, dengxiang grass, sand chives, wild leeks, juhuiliao, white mugwort, and salt-land pine nuts.
translations.idiomatic: Local produce included barley, lablab beans, highland barley, haozi, guziman, seeds of salt-land purslane, cistanche shoots, small elm fruits, mat-chicken grass seeds, rehmannia leaves, dengxiang grass, sand chives, wild leeks, juhuiliao, white mugwort, and salt-land pine nuts.

sentences.zh: 民年十五為丁。

translations.literal: At age fifteen the people became adult males liable for service.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen a man became liable for service.

sentences.zh: 有二丁者，取一為正軍。

translations.literal: Where there were two adult males, one was taken as a regular soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Households with two adult males furnished one regular soldier.

sentences.zh: 負擔雜使一人為抄，四丁為兩抄。

translations.literal: One porter and odd-job man formed a cao; four adult males formed two cao.
translations.idiomatic: One porter and laborer made a cao unit; four adult males made two cao.

sentences.zh: 餘人得射它丁，皆習戰鬥。

translations.literal: The remainder could be drafted from other adult males; all practiced fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The rest could be drawn from other households' adult males; all were trained for battle.

sentences.zh: 正軍馬駝各一，每家自置一帳。

translations.literal: Each regular soldier had one horse and one camel; each household set up its own tent.
translations.idiomatic: Each regular soldier had one horse and one camel; every household maintained its own tent.

sentences.zh: 團練使上，帳、弓、矢各一，馬五百疋，槖駝一，旗鼓五，槍、劍、棍棓、粆袋、雨氊、渾脫、鍬、钁、箭牌、鐵笊籬各一；

translations.literal: Above the militia commissioner: one tent, bow, and arrows each; five hundred horses; one Bactrian camel; five flags and drums; one each of spear, sword, club, bran bag, rain felt, inflated hide boat, spade, hoe, arrow shield, and iron rake;
translations.idiomatic: Officers from militia commissioner upward each had a tent, bow, and quiver; five hundred horses; one Bactrian camel; five sets of flags and drums; and one each of spear, sword, club, bran bag, rain felt, inflated hide boat, spade, hoe, arrow shield, and iron rake;

sentences.zh: 刺史以下，人各一駝，箭三百，毛幕一；

translations.literal: From prefect downward, each man had one camel, three hundred arrows, and one felt tent;
translations.idiomatic: From prefect downward, each man had one camel, three hundred arrows, and one felt tent;

sentences.zh: 餘兵三人共一幕。

translations.literal: the remaining soldiers shared one tent among three.
translations.idiomatic: ordinary soldiers shared one tent among three men.

sentences.zh: 有炮手二百人，號「潑喜」。

translations.literal: There were two hundred artillerymen called "Poxi."
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred artillerymen were called "Poxi".

sentences.zh: 勇健者號「撞令郎」。

translations.literal: The brave and strong were called "Zhuanglinglang."
translations.idiomatic: The bravest warriors were called "Zhuanglinglang".

sentences.zh: 賫糧不過一旬。

translations.literal: Provisions carried did not exceed ten days.
translations.idiomatic: They carried no more than ten days' rations.

sentences.zh: 晝則舉煙、揚塵，夜則篝火為候。

translations.literal: By day they raised smoke and dust; by night they lit beacon fires as signals.
translations.idiomatic: By day they signaled with smoke and dust; by night with beacon fires.

sentences.zh: 若獲人馬，射之，號曰殺鬼招魂。

translations.literal: If they captured men or horses, they shot them, calling it killing ghosts and summoning souls.
translations.idiomatic: When they took men or horses captive, they shot them in a rite called "killing ghosts and summoning souls."

sentences.zh: 或射草縛人。

translations.literal: Or they shot at straw figures bound like men.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes they shot at straw figures bound like men instead.

sentences.zh: 出軍用單日，避晦日。

translations.literal: They took the field on odd-numbered days and avoided the last day of the month.
translations.idiomatic: They marched out on odd-numbered days and avoided the last day of the month.

sentences.zh: 多立虛寨，設伏兵。

translations.literal: They often set up dummy camps and laid ambushes.
translations.idiomatic: They often erected decoy camps and laid ambushes.

sentences.zh: 衣重甲，乘善馬，以鐵騎為前鋒，用鉤索絞聯，雖死馬上不落。

translations.literal: They wore heavy armor, rode good horses, used iron cavalry as vanguard, linked themselves with hook ropes, and even when dead did not fall from the horse.
translations.idiomatic: They wore heavy armor and rode fine horses; iron cavalry led the van, linked by hook ropes so that even the dead did not fall from the saddle.

sentences.zh: 其民俗勇悍，衣冠、騎乘、土產品物、子姓傳國，亦略知其大概耳。

translations.literal: Their people's custom was brave and fierce; as for dress and caps, riding, local products, and succession of the surname in ruling the state, one also knows the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Their people were by nature fierce and warlike; their dress, mounts, local products, and dynastic succession are known only in broad outline.

sentences.zh: 初，西夏臣宋有年，賜姓曰趙；

translations.literal: At first Western Xia had been subjects of Song for many years and were granted the surname Zhao;
translations.idiomatic: At first Western Xia had long been subject to Song and bore the granted surname Zhao;

sentences.zh: 迨遼聖宗統和四年，繼遷叛宋，始來附遼，授特進檢校太師、都督夏州諸軍事，遂復姓李。

translations.literal: when in the fourth year of Tonghe of Emperor Shengzong of Liao, Jiqian rebelled against Song and first came to attach to Liao, he was appointed Special Advancement Honorary Grand Preceptor and Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs of Xia Prefecture, and then resumed the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: but in the fourth year of Tonghe under Emperor Shengzong, Jiqian rebelled against Song and submitted to Liao; the court appointed him Special Advancement Honorary Grand Preceptor and commander of all military affairs in Xia Prefecture, and he resumed the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 十月，遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, envoys were sent to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Western Xia sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 六年，入貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, they sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 七年，來貢，以王子帳耶律襄之女封義成公主，下嫁繼遷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, they came to offer tribute; the daughter of Yelu Xiang of the Prince's Account was enfeoffed as Princess Yicheng and given in marriage to Jiqian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, they sent tribute; a daughter of Yelu Xiang of the Prince's Account was enfeoffed as Princess Yicheng and given to Jiqian in marriage.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，來謝。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year, they came to offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year, they came to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 三月，又來貢。

translations.literal: In the third month, they came to offer tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, tribute came again.

sentences.zh: 九月，繼遷遣使獻宋俘。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Jiqian sent envoys presenting Song captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Jiqian sent envoys presenting captives taken from Song.

sentences.zh: 十月，以敗宋軍來告。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, they came to report defeating the Song army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, they reported a victory over the Song army.

sentences.zh: 十二月，下宋麟、鄜等州，來告，遣使封繼遷為夏國王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, having taken the Song prefectures of Lin and Fu and others, they came to report; envoys were sent to enfeoff Jiqian as King of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, having captured the Song prefectures of Lin, Fu, and others, they sent word; the court dispatched envoys to invest Jiqian as King of Xia.

sentences.zh: 九年二月，遣使告伐宋之捷。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year, envoys were sent to report victory in the campaign against Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the ninth year, they reported victory in the campaign against Song.

sentences.zh: 四月，遣李知白來謝封冊。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Li Zhibai was sent to thank for the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Li Zhibai was sent to thank the court for the investiture.

sentences.zh: 七月，復綏、銀二州，來告。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Sui and Yin prefectures were recovered; they came to report.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, they recovered Sui and Yin prefectures and sent word.

sentences.zh: 十月，繼遷以宋所授敕命，遣使來上。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Jiqian sent the commission and edict granted by Song; envoys came to present them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Jiqian sent the commission and edict Song had granted him for presentation to the Liao court.

sentences.zh: 是月，定難軍節度使李繼捧來附，授開府儀同三司、檢校太師，兼侍中，封西平王，仍賜推忠效順啟聖定難功臣。

translations.literal: That month, Li Jipeng, military commissioner of Dingnan Army, came to submit; he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, Honorary Grand Preceptor, and Concurrent Palace Attendant, enfeoffed as Western Peace Prince, and still granted the title Meritorious Minister for Loyalty, Submission, and Opening Sagacity in Pacifying Difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: That same month, Li Jipeng, military commissioner of the Dingnan Army, submitted; the court appointed him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, Honorary Grand Preceptor, and Concurrent Palace Attendant, enfeoffed him as Prince of Western Peace, and granted him the title Meritorious Minister for Loyal Submission and Pacification.

sentences.zh: 十二月，繼遷潛附於宋，遣韓德威持詔諭之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Jiqian secretly attached to Song; Han Dewei was sent bearing an edict to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Jiqian was discovered secretly dealing with Song; Han Dewei was sent with an edict to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 十年二月，韓德威還，奏繼遷托故不出，至靈州俘掠以還。

translations.literal: In the second month of the tenth year, Han Dewei returned and reported that Jiqian made excuses and would not come out, and that he went as far as Ling Prefecture, seized captives and plunder, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the tenth year, Han Dewei returned and reported that Jiqian had made excuses and refused to appear, then raided as far as Ling Prefecture and returned with captives and booty.

sentences.zh: 西夏遣使來奏德威俘掠，賜詔撫諭。

translations.literal: Western Xia sent envoys to report Dewei's seizure and plunder; an edict was bestowed to comfort and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: Western Xia sent envoys complaining of Dewei's raid; the court issued an edict of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 十月，來貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Western Xia sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二年，入貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, Goryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十三年，敗宋師，遣使來告。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, they defeated the Song army and sent envoys to report.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, they defeated a Song army and sent word.

sentences.zh: 十四年，又來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, they came to offer tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, tribute came again.

sentences.zh: 十五年三月，以破宋兵來告，封繼遷為西平王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year, having defeated Song troops they came to report; Jiqian was enfeoffed as Western Peace Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifteenth year, they reported a victory over Song forces, and Jiqian was enfeoffed as Prince of Western Peace.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣使來謝封冊。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, envoys were sent to thank for the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, they sent envoys to thank the court for the investiture.

sentences.zh: 十六年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, Goryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授繼遷子德明朔方軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Jiqian's son Deming was appointed military commissioner of Shuofang Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, Jiqian's son Deming was appointed military commissioner of the Shuofang Army.

sentences.zh: 十九年，遣李文冀來貢。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Li Wenji was sent to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, Li Wenji was sent with tribute.

sentences.zh: 六月，奏下宋恒、環、慶三州，賜詔褒美。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, they memorialized having taken the three Song prefectures of Heng, Huan, and Qing; an edict was bestowed praising them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, they reported the capture of the Song prefectures of Heng, Huan, and Qing; the court issued an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遣使來進馬、駝。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, envoys were sent presenting horses and camels.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, they sent horses and camels as tribute.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣劉仁勖來告下靈州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Liu Renxu was sent to report the taking of Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Liu Renxu was sent to report the capture of Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，繼遷薨，其子德昭遣使來告。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Jiqian died; his son Dezhao sent envoys to report it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, Jiqian died; his son Dezhao sent envoys to announce his death.

sentences.zh: 六月，贈繼遷尚書令，遣西上閣門使丁振吊慰。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Jiqian was posthumously granted Minister of the Masters of Writing; Western Upper Gate Commissioner Ding Zhen was sent to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Jiqian was posthumously made Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Western Upper Gate Commissioner Ding Zhen was sent to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 八月，德昭遣使來謝吊贈。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Dezhao sent envoys to thank for the condolences and posthumous grant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Dezhao sent envoys to thank the court for the condolences and posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 二十二年三月，德昭遣使上繼遷遺留物。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-second year, Dezhao sent envoys presenting objects Jiqian had left behind.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-second year, Dezhao sent the goods Jiqian had left behind.

sentences.zh: 七月，封德昭為西平王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Dezhao was enfeoffed as Western Peace Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Dezhao was enfeoffed as Prince of Western Peace.

sentences.zh: 十月，遣使來謝封冊。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, envoys were sent to thank for the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, they sent envoys to thank the court for the investiture.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，下宋青城，來告。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, they took Song's Qingcheng and came to report.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, they captured Qingcheng from Song and sent word.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，德昭母薨，遣使吊祭，起復。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Dezhao's mother died; envoys were sent to offer mourning sacrifices, and mourning leave was ended.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, Dezhao's mother died; the court sent envoys to perform mourning rites and ordered Dezhao to leave mourning.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，承天皇太后崩，遣使報哀於夏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Empress Dowager Chengtian died; envoys were sent to announce the mourning to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, Empress Dowager Chengtian died, and envoys were sent to announce the mourning to Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遣使冊德昭為夏國王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, envoys were sent to invest Dezhao as King of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, envoys were sent to invest Dezhao as King of Xia.

sentences.zh: 開泰元年，德昭遣使進良馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaitai, Dezhao sent envoys presenting fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaitai, Dezhao sent fine horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣使引進使李延弘賜夏國王李德昭及義成公主車馬。

translations.literal: In the second year, Introducing Commissioner Li Yanhong was sent to bestow carriages and horses on King of Xia Li Dezhao and Princess Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Introducing Commissioner Li Yanhong was sent to present carriages and horses to King Li Dezhao of Xia and Princess Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 太平元年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiping, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiping, Western Xia sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十一年，聖宗崩，報哀於夏，德昭遣使來進賻幣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Emperor Shengzong died; mourning was announced to Xia, and Dezhao sent envoys presenting funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Emperor Shengzong died; the court announced the mourning to Western Xia, and Dezhao sent funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 興宗即位，以興平公主下嫁李元昊，以元昊為駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xingzong succeeded, Princess Xingping was given in marriage to Li Yuanhao, and Yuanhao was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xingzong succeeded, Princess Xingping was given in marriage to Li Yuanhao, who was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 重熙元年，夏國遣使來賀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongxi, the Xia state sent envoys to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongxi, Western Xia sent envoys to congratulate the new reign.

sentences.zh: 李德昭薨，冊其子夏國公元昊為王。

translations.literal: Li Dezhao died; his son, King of Xia Li Yuanhao, was invested as king.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dezhao died, and his son Yuanhao, Duke of Xia, was invested as king.

sentences.zh: 二年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Goryeo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二月，禁夏國使沿路私市金鐵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xia envoys were forbidden to trade gold and iron privately along the route.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, private trade in gold and iron along the route was forbidden to Xia envoys.

sentences.zh: 七年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, they sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 李元昊與平公主不諧，公主薨，遣北院承旨耶律庶成持詔問之。

translations.literal: Li Yuanhao and Princess Ping were not harmonious; when the princess died, Northern Court Drafter Yelu Shucheng was sent bearing an edict to question him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanhao and Princess Ping were estranged; when the princess died, Northern Court Drafter Yelu Shucheng was sent with an edict to question him.

sentences.zh: 九年，宋遣郭禎以伐夏來報。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Song sent Guo Zhen to report the campaign against Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Song sent Guo Zhen to inform Liao of its campaign against Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 十年，夏國獻所俘宋將及生口。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Xia state presented Song generals and captives taken alive whom they had seized.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Western Xia presented Song generals and captives it had taken.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遣使問宋興師伐夏之由。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, envoys were sent to ask Song the reason for raising troops to attack Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Liao sent envoys to ask Song why it had launched a campaign against Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 十二月，禁吐渾鬻馬於夏，沿邊築障塞以防之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Tuyuhun were forbidden to sell horses to Xia, and barrier defenses were built along the border to guard against it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, the Tuyuhun were forbidden to sell horses to Western Xia, and barrier defenses were built along the frontier to enforce the ban.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，遣同知析津府事耶律敵烈、樞密都承旨王惟吉諭夏國與宋和。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year, Associate Administrator of Xijin Prefecture Yelu Dilie and Privy Council Chief Drafter Wang Weiji were sent to instruct the Xia state to make peace with Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year, Yelu Dilie, associate administrator of Xijin Prefecture, and Wang Weiji, chief drafter of the Privy Council, were sent to urge Western Xia to make peace with Song.

sentences.zh: 二月，元昊以加上尊號，遣使來賀。

translations.literal: In the second month, Yuanhao, on account of the bestowal of an honorific title, sent envoys to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Yuanhao sent envoys to congratulate the court on the bestowal of an honorific title.

sentences.zh: 耶律敵烈等使夏國還，奏元昊罷兵，遣使報宋。

translations.literal: When Yelu Dilie and the others returned from their mission to Xia, they reported that Yuanhao had ceased hostilities and sent envoys to inform Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Yelu Dilie and his party returned from Western Xia, they reported that Yuanhao had halted hostilities and sent envoys to notify Song.

sentences.zh: 四月，夏國遣使進馬、駝。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the Xia state sent envoys presenting horses and camels.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Western Xia sent horses and camels as tribute.

sentences.zh: 七月，元昊上表請伐宋，不從。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Yuanhao submitted a memorial requesting permission to attack Song; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Yuanhao petitioned for permission to attack Song; the request was refused.

sentences.zh: 十月，夏人侵党項，遣延昌宮使高家奴讓之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the Xia people invaded the Tangut; Yanchang Palace Commissioner Gao Jianu was sent to reprove them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Western Xia raided the Tangut; Yanchang Palace Commissioner Gao Jianu was sent to rebuke them.

sentences.zh: 十三年四月，党項及山西部族節度使屈烈以五部叛入西夏，詔征諸道兵討之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year, the Tangut and Qu Lie, military commissioner of the Western Mountain Tribes, led five divisions in rebellion into Western Xia; an edict ordered troops from all circuits to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year, the Tangut and Qu Lie, military commissioner of the Western Mountain tribes, led five divisions in revolt into Western Xia; the court ordered troops from all circuits to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 六月，阻卜酋長烏八遣其子執元昊所遣求援使窊邑改來。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Zubu chieftain Wuba sent his son escorting Wayigai, the envoy Yuanhao had sent to seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Zubu chieftain Wuba sent his son escorting Wayigai, the envoy Yuanhao had dispatched to seek aid.

sentences.zh: 八月，夏使對不以情，羈之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Xia envoy answered without sincerity and was detained.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, a Xia envoy gave evasive answers and was detained.

sentences.zh: 使復來，詢事宜不實對，笞之。

translations.literal: When the envoy came again and was questioned about affairs but answered untruthfully, he was flogged.
translations.idiomatic: When another envoy came and gave false answers to questions about the situation, he was flogged.

sentences.zh: 十月，元昊上表謝罪，欲收集叛黨以獻，從之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Yuanhao submitted a memorial apologizing and wishing to gather the rebels to present them; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Yuanhao submitted a memorial of apology, offering to round up the rebels and hand them over; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 進方物，命北院樞密副使蕭革迓之。

translations.literal: He presented local products; Northern Privy Deputy Commissioner Xiao Ge was ordered to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent local products as tribute, and Northern Privy Deputy Commissioner Xiao Ge was ordered to receive him.

sentences.zh: 元昊親率党項三部來降，詰其納叛背盟，元昊伏罪。

translations.literal: Yuanhao personally led three Tangut divisions to submit; he was questioned for harboring rebels and breaking the alliance, and Yuanhao confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao personally led three Tangut divisions to submit; rebuked for harboring rebels and breaking the alliance, he confessed his guilt.

sentences.zh: 初，夏人執蕭胡睹，至是，請以被執者來歸。

translations.literal: Earlier the Xia people had seized Xiao Huzhu; at this time they requested that those seized be returned.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Western Xia had seized Xiao Huzhu; now they asked that their own detained envoys be returned.

sentences.zh: 詔所留夏使亦還其國。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the detained Xia envoys also to be returned to their state.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the detained Xia envoys sent home as well.

sentences.zh: 十二月，胡睹來歸，又遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Huzhu returned, and envoys were again sent to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Huzhu was released, and Western Xia again sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十七年，元昊薨，其子諒祚遣使來告，上其父遺留物。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Yuanhao died; his son Liangzuo sent envoys to report it and presented his father's leftover goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, Yuanhao died; his son Liangzuo sent word and presented his father's remaining goods.

sentences.zh: 鐵不得國乞以本部軍助攻夏國，不許。

translations.literal: The Tiedebuduo state begged to use its own troops to assist in attacking the Xia state; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiedebuduo state asked to join the attack on Western Xia with its own forces; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 十八年，復議伐夏，留其賀正使不遣，遣北院樞密副使蕭惟信以伐夏告宋。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, a campaign against Xia was again discussed; their New Year's congratulatory envoy was detained and not sent back; Northern Privy Deputy Commissioner Xiao Weixin was sent to inform Song of the campaign against Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, the court again debated a campaign against Western Xia; it detained the Xia New Year's envoy and sent Northern Privy Deputy Commissioner Xiao Weixin to inform Song of the planned attack.

sentences.zh: 六月，夏國遣使來貢，留之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Xia state sent envoys to offer tribute; they were detained.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Western Xia sent tribute envoys, who were detained.

sentences.zh: 七月，親征。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the emperor campaigned in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, the emperor led the campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 八月，渡河，夏人遁。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, he crossed the river and the Xia people fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he crossed the river, and the Xia forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 九月，蕭惠為夏人所敗。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Xiao Hui was defeated by the Xia people.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Xiao Hui was defeated by Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 十月，招討使耶律敵古率阻卜軍至賀蘭山，獲元昊妻及其官屬。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Pacification Commissioner Yelu Digu led Zubu troops to Helan Mountain and captured Yuanhao's wife and his officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Pacification Commissioner Yelu Digu led Zubu troops to Helan Mountain and captured Yuanhao's wife and his officials.

sentences.zh: 遇其軍三千來拒，殪之；

translations.literal: They met three thousand of their troops coming to resist and destroyed them;
translations.idiomatic: They met three thousand enemy troops and annihilated them;

sentences.zh: 詳穩蕭慈氏奴、南剋耶律斡里歿于陣。

translations.literal: detailed commanders Xiao Cisinu and Yelu Wol of Nank perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: detailed commanders Xiao Cisinu and Yelu Wol of Nank fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 十九年正月，遣使問罪於夏。

translations.literal: In the first month of the nineteenth year, envoys were sent to demand accountability from Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the nineteenth year, envoys were sent to demand an accounting from Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 夏將窪普等攻金肅城，耶律高家奴等破之，窪普被創遁去，殺猥貨乙靈紀。

translations.literal: Xia generals Wapu and others attacked Jinsu City; Yelu Gao Jianu and others defeated them; Wapu was wounded and fled; Weihuo Yilingji was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xia generals led by Wapu attacked Jinsu City; Yelu Gao Jianu and others routed them; Wapu was wounded and fled, and Weihuo Yilingji was killed.

sentences.zh: 三月，殿前都點檢蕭叠裏得與夏軍戰於三角川，敗之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Palace Front Commander Xiao Dielide fought the Xia army at Triangle River and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Palace Front Commander Xiao Dielide defeated the Xia army at Triangle River.

sentences.zh: 招討使蕭蒲奴、北院大王宜新等帥師伐夏，都部署別古得為監戰。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Xiao Punu, Northern Court King Yixin, and others led troops to attack Xia; Mobile Command Director Biegude was battle overseer.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Xiao Punu, Northern Court King Yixin, and others led a campaign against Western Xia, with Mobile Command Director Biegude as battle overseer.

sentences.zh: 五月，蕭蒲奴等入夏境，不遇敵，縱軍俘掠而還。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Xiao Punu and others entered Xia territory, met no enemy, let the army seize captives and plunder, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Xiao Punu and his forces entered Xia territory, met no resistance, plundered freely, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夏國窪普來降。

translations.literal: Xia state's Wapu came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Wapu of Western Xia came over to the Liao side.

sentences.zh: 十月，李諒祚母遣使乞依舊稱臣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Li Liangzuo's mother sent envoys begging to submit as a subject as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Li Liangzuo's mother sent envoys pleading to resume former subject status.

sentences.zh: 十二月，諒祚上表如母訓。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Liangzuo submitted a memorial as his mother had instructed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Liangzuo submitted a memorial following his mother's instructions.

sentences.zh: 二十年二月，遣使索党項叛戶。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twentieth year, envoys were sent to demand the Tangut rebel households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twentieth year, envoys were sent to demand the return of Tangut rebel households.

sentences.zh: 五月，蕭爻括使夏回，進諒祚母表，乞代党項權進馬駝牛羊等物；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Xiao Yaoguo returned from his mission to Xia and presented a memorial from Liangzuo's mother, begging to present horses, camels, cattle, and sheep on behalf of the Tangut provisionally;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Xiao Yaoguo returned from Western Xia with a memorial from Liangzuo's mother, asking to present horses, camels, cattle, and sheep on the Tangut's behalf;

sentences.zh: 又求唐隆鎮，仍乞罷所建城邑。

translations.literal: she also requested Tanglong garrison and still begged that the walled towns that had been built be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: she also asked for Tanglong garrison and for the abandonment of the walled towns Liao had built.

sentences.zh: 以詔答之。

translations.literal: An edict was issued in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The court answered with an edict.

sentences.zh: 六月，獲元昊妻，及俘到夏人置於蘇州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Yuanhao's wife was captured, and Xia captives taken were placed in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Yuanhao's wife was captured, and Xia prisoners were settled in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十一年十月，諒祚遣使乞弛邊備，遣爻括賫詔諭之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-first year, Liangzuo sent envoys begging that border defenses be relaxed; Yaoguo was sent bearing an edict to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twenty-first year, Liangzuo asked that border defenses be relaxed; Xiao Yaoguo was sent with an edict in reply.

sentences.zh: 二十二年七月，諒祚進降表，遣林牙高家奴賫詔撫諭。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-second year, Liangzuo submitted a surrender memorial; Palace Attendant Gao Jianu was sent bearing an edict to comfort and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-second year, Liangzuo submitted a surrender memorial; Palace Attendant Gao Jianu was sent with an edict of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 二十三年正月，貢方物。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-third year, local products were offered as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-third year, Western Xia sent local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 五月，乞進馬駝，詔歲貢之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, they begged to present horses and camels; an edict ordered annual tribute of them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, they asked to present horses and camels; the court decreed annual tribute.

sentences.zh: 七月，諒祚遣使求婚。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Liangzuo sent envoys requesting a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Liangzuo sent envoys to request a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 十月，進誓表。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, an oath memorial was presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, he submitted an oath of allegiance.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，興宗崩，遣使報哀於夏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Emperor Xingzong died; envoys were sent to announce the mourning to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, Emperor Xingzong died, and envoys were sent to announce the mourning to Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 道宗即位，清寧元年，遣使來賀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daozong succeeded, in the first year of Qingning envoys were sent to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daozong succeeded, Western Xia sent envoys in the first year of Qingning to congratulate him.

sentences.zh: 九月，以先帝遺物賜夏。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, objects left by the late emperor were bestowed on Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the court bestowed goods left by the late emperor on Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，遣使會葬。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, envoys were sent to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year, they sent envoys to attend the funeral.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，禁民鬻銅於夏。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year, the people were forbidden to sell copper to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year, private sale of copper to Western Xia was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 咸雍元年五月，來貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Xianyong, they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Xianyong, Western Xia sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月，遣使進回鶻僧、金佛、《梵覺經》。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year, envoys were sent presenting Uyghur monks, a gold Buddha, and the Fanjue Sutra.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year, they sent Uyghur monks, a gold Buddha, and the Fanjue Sutra as tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二月，諒祚薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Liangzuo died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Liangzuo died.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，諒祚子秉常遣使報哀，即遣使吊祭。
